subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a cleric who cannot utter his god's name in the temple, resulting in his prayers manifesting as complaints and despair; he was severely injured after slaying a wraith with divine radiance and is now being carried away from the battlefield by Dren's mercenaries, deemed too vulnerable to continue fighting.
source_quote: I am the boss. Yes, I am. And the boss does not run from evil. But they carried me anyway...

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a pragmatic, ruthless leader who manipulates factions into civil war to seize control of the Greater Temple; he brokers a deal with Kelno, accepts his intelligence network and goblins, and strategically removes Calmer from combat to preserve his own operational autonomy.
source_quote: We are the victors... This is starting to be a very lucrative operation.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a blunt, observant member of Zephyr’s inner circle who voices the group’s cynical realism; he recognizes the power dynamics of the temple war and affirms their position as the inevitable victors through calculated inaction and exploitation.
source_quote: We are the victors.

subject: Dren
fact: Dren is a mercenary captain who remains loyal to Zephyr and his team despite the treacherous environment; he carries out orders without question and is entrusted with guarding Calmer, the only person in the temple whose loyalty cannot be bought.
source_quote: You didn't put me in charge of mercenaries, because I tell you what to do.

subject: Kelno
fact: Kelno is an elderly, cunning prophet of air who has survived multiple temple wars by aligning with the strongest faction; he offers Zephyr control of his intelligence network in exchange for partnership, revealing he anticipated the war and prepared the second chair for Zephyr weeks in advance.
source_quote: I've noted for a week... You are going to be the one.

subject: The Greater Temple
fact: The Greater Temple is the ruling body of the temple complex, whose leadership is determined by survival in a cycle of civil war; its doors open only after the lesser temples have fought to exhaustion, and the victor inherits control of all resources and informants.
source_quote: When the war ended, the great doors would open, and whoever stood on top of the upper temple became the Greater Temple's new partner.

subject: The Four Lesser Temples
fact: The four lesser temples — Earth, Air, Fire, and Water — are competing factions whose leaders are being systematically eliminated through assassination, betrayal, and internal conflict orchestrated by Zephyr’s group; each has its own treasury, mercenaries, and methods of operation.
source_quote: The Fire Temple folding inward. Water Temple knives at the captain's threshold.

subject: Slaying of the Wraith
fact: Calmer used divine radiance to kill a wraith twice, each time the power failing as it encountered no recognition — an act that drained him physically and spiritually, leaving him injured and unable to continue in combat.
source_quote: The wraith was dead... I had been the one to kill it. Twice it had laughed at the holy power I called down in His name.

subject: Assassination of Hartsch
fact: Hartsch, a key leader of the Fire Temple, was assassinated by Belsornig’s agents, triggering a cascade of violence that allowed Zephyr’s group to position themselves as the dominant power in the temple complex.
source_quote: Assassins had reached Hartsch's antechamber an hour ago. By tonight our puppet would be meat.

subject: Zephyr’s Pact with Kelno
fact: Zephyr accepted Kelno’s offer to become his second-in-command, gaining access to his network of goblins, informants, and intelligence; in return, Kelno secured his survival by aligning with the rising power.
source_quote: His goblins, mine. His informants, mine. The throne, mine. His little office, his.

subject: Removal of Calmer from the Battlefield
fact: Calmer was carried away from the Air Temple by Dren’s mercenaries at Zephyr’s indirect behest, ensuring he would not interfere with the final moves of the war — a decision that preserved Calmer’s life but removed him from agency.
source_quote: Calmer wasn't with us. Deeply injured, parked with Dren's mercenaries somewhere behind a curtain so he wouldn't get himself killed...

subject: Battle for the Water Temple
fact: With the Fire Temple leader dead and the Earth Temple leader removed, Zephyr’s group prepares to strike the Water Temple, now lightly guarded, to complete their takeover of the temple complex.
source_quote: He pointed us toward the Water Temple — lightly guarded now, he observed, as good a time as any to strike.

subject: The Second Chair
fact: Kelno had placed a second chair in his chamber two weeks before Zephyr’s arrival, symbolizing his expectation that a new power would rise; its presence confirmed his foresight and willingness to submit to whoever proved strongest.
source_quote: A little note that said *set out the second chair* — two weeks old.

subject: The Ledger of Payments
fact: Kelno’s ledger contained records of bribes paid to a dozen names, revealing his long-term control over temple politics; the ledger was the physical proof of his influence and the foundation of the deal he offered Zephyr.
source_quote: A ledger. Payments out to a dozen names.

subject: Calmer’s Loss of Faith
fact: Calmer’s inability to speak his god’s name in the temple has eroded his spiritual authority and rendered his divine power unreliable; his internal struggle mirrors his physical removal from the war, suggesting a deeper collapse of identity and purpose.
source_quote: I said it to the dark anyway, the way I'd been saying His name to the dark for weeks now — quiet, where no one could hear, where it couldn't blow my cover...

subject: The Nature of Victory
fact: Zephyr’s group has won not through direct conquest but by orchestrating the self-destruction of rival factions; the question remains whether their victory is sustainable, or merely the next stage in the temple’s endless cycle of betrayal.
source_quote: One does not simply take bribes to defect and end up the rightful lords of anything. We ended up here anyway.

subject: The Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple is Kelno’s stronghold, a gray, lifeless chamber filled with skulls, mead, and scrolls; it serves as the site of Zephyr’s pivotal alliance and the last place Calmer was conscious before being removed.
source_quote: The room the color of old ash... skulls. Human, demi-human, arranged like a man arranges things he's stopped thinking about.

subject: The Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple is the next target of Zephyr’s group, now lightly guarded after the collapse of the Fire Temple; it represents the final obstacle to total control of the temple complex and the next stage of their ascent.
source_quote: He pointed us toward the Water Temple — lightly guarded now, he observed, as good a time as any to strike.

subject: The Upper Temple
fact: The Upper Temple is the seat of ultimate authority, whose doors only open after the lesser temples have fought to exhaustion; its control is the prize Zephyr seeks, and its threshold is where Calmer was dragged away from, symbolizing his exclusion from power.
source_quote: Whoever stood on top of the upper temple became the Greater Temple's new partner.

subject: The Wraith
fact: The wraith was a spectral entity that resisted divine power, laughing at Calmer’s holy radiance until it was destroyed; its defeat cost Calmer dearly and marked the beginning of his physical and spiritual decline.
source_quote: Twice the holy radiance had hit the wraith and simply ceased — the way divine light ceases when it finds nothing that recognizes it.

subject: Two Weeks Ago
fact: Two weeks before Zephyr’s arrival, Kelno set out the second chair, anticipating the rise of a new power; this temporal marker confirms his long-term planning and the inevitability of the war that followed.
source_quote: A little note that said *set out the second chair* — two weeks old.
